blockers.summary: CE438 stands at the inside node of cut-north-up-main, facing into play, and OSM gives it no railway:signal:<category> tag, so its function is unknown and movement never passes it (D-033). Every Up Main entry from the north (rt-um-fringe-ce336) stops there.
blockers.needed: A source stating CE438's function: an OSM category tag from survey, or a signalling plan
blockers.proposedChange: If CE438 is a main signal, split rt-um-fringe-ce336 at it (fringe -> CE438, CE438 -> CE336); if it is a repeater or distant, no route change. Neither is assumed.

blockers.summary: CE263 stands at the inside node of cut-wcml-south-up, facing out of play towards Penrith, with no OSM category: any Up Main exit to the south would have to pass it, so none can be run.
blockers.needed: A source stating CE263's function (OSM category tag from survey, or a signalling plan)
blockers.proposedChange: If main: an exit route CE263 -> fringe on cut-wcml-south-up; if a repeater/distant: the exit route may start at the previous Up main signal. Both also need B-CE268, B-UPMAIN-UNTYPED and B-UPMAIN-DIAMOND.

blockers.summary: CE268 on the Up Main south of CE278 faces southbound trains and has no OSM category, so no Up route can pass it.
blockers.proposedChange: Split or end the Up Main exit routes at CE268 once its function is sourced.

blockers.summary: South of CE304 the Up Main passes osm-n2464365978 and osm-n13915496837: nodes with three edges and no railway=switch tag, so the importer creates no Points record and no game rule can configure them (D-029). Treating them as switches would invent topology.
blockers.needed: OSM tagging of the two junctions (survey or imagery), or a signalling diagram
blockers.proposedChange: Correct the OSM tagging and re-import (infrastructure.json is generated, never hand-edited); then simple game rules and Up Main routes CE304 -> CE285 -> CE278 -> ... can be authored.

blockers.summary: The Up Main south of CE304 crosses diamond osm-n3057659458 (OSM railway=railway_crossing). The game-rule model cannot configure crossings (D-029 limit), so a route over it stays unresolved.
blockers.needed: A model decision: game-rule crossing passages (straight across, paired by continuous OSM ways, as I-012 does for slips), with conflicts at the crossing declared
blockers.proposedChange: Extend GameRules with crossing rules and the C4 conflict check; a schema and validator change for a later phase.

blockers.summary: Diamond osm-n1051241139 at Petteril Bridge Jn is crossed by the Down Newcastle (from cut-newcastle-down, just past CE379) and the Up Midland (to cut-midland-up). Every Tyne Valley arrival and every Settle-Carlisle departure crosses it; crossings cannot be configured (D-029).

Platform 1's only southern connection passes osm-n1460504022, tagged railway=switch but mapped with two edges (a leg is missing; D-025): movements through it are unresolved, so platform 1 is reachable from the north cuts only. No OSM signal is mapped on platform 1 either.
blockers.needed: Imagery or an OSM check of the switch's missing leg, then a re-import
blockers.proposedChange: After an OSM correction and re-import: game rules for the switch and double slip osm-n1460504024 (movement list), and a route from CE286 through platform 1 joining the Down Main at osm-n3720819849.

blockers.summary: OSM maps no signal on the platform 5 and 6 bay tracks (D-020), so no route can start there. Absence in OSM does not show that no real signal exists.
blockers.needed: Survey or a signalling plan locating the bay starting signals
blockers.proposedChange: Add the signals to OSM (survey) and re-import; then starting routes from bays 5 and 6.

blockers.summary: From buffer stop to first signal or junction the bays measure: platform 2 133.7 m (CE302), 7 151.3 m (CE327), 8 151.1 m (CE328), 6 181.9 m. The session's game train is 200 m; real formations are unknown (CIF timing load and length are not imported), so no train can be placed in these bays at the default setting.
blockers.needed: Train length per service (CIF BS timing load import plus a formation source), or an owner decision on a shorter game length
blockers.proposedChange: Import CIF timing load/length data; never shorten a train to fit a bay without a source or an explicit game setting.

blockers.summary: A service whose first call is in play has no call before play, so the planner cannot give it an entry (P5 requires a call either side of the area block). Placing a train at its origin platform would need where its stock comes from (associations, empty workings), which is not modelled.
blockers.needed: A design for in-area origins: placement on proven-clear platform track, formation from an association or a stabled train, and the starting signal's route
blockers.proposedChange: A later phase: an origin placement mode in the plan and service-entry stage, with associations; not done in P6.

blockers.summary: A service whose last call is in play has no exit fringe: it must stop and remain at a platform, form another service, or be shunted away. Routes ending at a buffer stop or platform, train stabling and reversal are not modelled.
blockers.needed: A design for terminating trains: stopping positions, stabling, associations (next workings) and reversal
blockers.proposedChange: A later phase; never remove a terminating train from play to make it count as complete.

blockers.summary: The service calls at a Kingmoor yard TIPLOC (deferred area, D-018). Which line and north cut it uses to reach or leave the yard (CIF lines UA, DA, GL at Kingmoor Jn lie beyond the cuts) is not audited, and a service that starts or ends in the deferred area has no call on the far side of play.
blockers.needed: An audit of the Kingmoor yard connections beyond the north cuts, and an owner decision on Kingmoor handover (D-018)
blockers.proposedChange: Patterns that leave or enter play at the north goods cuts for yard workings, once the handover is decided; no Kingmoor yard simulation.

blockers.summary: The service passes through the area more than once; the planner maps one contiguous block of area calls only.
blockers.needed: A design for repeated visits (and the reversals they imply)

blockers.summary: London Road Jn (CARLLRJ) and Petteril Bridge Jn (PETLBGJ) have no infrastructure mapping, and which east cut each eastern TIPLOC uses rests on the cuts' inferred destinations (CORPUS: WETHERL Wetheral, WETHCOR Corby Gates (Tyne Valley); HOWEACS Cumwhinton (Settle-Carlisle))
blockers.needed: Sourced TIPLOC-to-infrastructure mappings (I-002 method) or a line diagram
blockers.proposedChange: Inferred timing-point positions for CARLLRJ and PETLBGJ, then east patterns.

blockers.summary: The Cumbrian Coast cuts (A and B) have no track ref or traffic direction in the dataset (both OSM ways carry preferred_direction=forward, not assessed in P6), Currock Jn (CARLCUR) is unmapped, and the two-edge switches at Bog Jn (osm-n314950822 and others) leave its connection to the south and east unresolved.
blockers.needed: Track identity and direction for the two Cumbrian Coast tracks; the Bog Jn survey item
blockers.proposedChange: Assess the preferred_direction tags and way order of the two cut edges; then fringes and routes to platform 2 and through.

blockers.summary: Goods lines avoiding the station via Upperby (CARLUBJ, CARLUJN, CARLUTG, CARLLSL, CARLUES) were not traced in P6; their TIPLOCs are unmapped.
blockers.needed: A topology audit of the Upperby goods lines and their signals, and TIPLOC mappings
blockers.proposedChange: A later audit; few services (3 through, 3 starting or terminating).

blockers.summary: The service matches no movement group in this table, so its movement has not been audited.
blockers.needed: A movement group for it in this table
blockers.proposedChange: Extend the table; the coverage test requires this group to stay empty.

blockers.summary: CIF platform codes A, B and C at CARLILE match no OSM platform ref (OSM has platforms 1-8 and one unnumbered outline); what they denote is unknown.
blockers.needed: A source for Carlisle's CIF platform codes (e.g. the Sectional Appendix or a station plan)
blockers.proposedChange: Map the codes only once sourced; never guess a platform.
